collection: NECO BECE National Values Education JSS 3 original objective practice
note: Original practice. Topic mappings use the historical July 2018 curriculum provisionally. Four options are an author practice choice. Current NECO content, paper allocation and curriculum adoption remain unverified.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Identify responsible conduct and its consequences in a work setting.
questions.prompt: A school-store volunteer finds that a delivery contains fewer exercise books than the receipt records. What should the volunteer do before signing the receipt?
options: Sign because the supplier is a family friend.
Record the difference and ask the supervising teacher to check it.
Change the stock book to match the receipt.
Accept the delivery and pay for the missing books secretly.
questions.answer: Record the difference and ask the supervising teacher to check it.
questions.explanation: Checking and openly recording the discrepancy protects accurate records and shows honesty.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Identify responsible conduct and its consequences in a work setting.
questions.prompt: At a workshop, Binta arrives before opening time but leaves assigned tools scattered after every session. Which judgement is best supported?
options: Punctuality alone proves that she completes all duties responsibly.
Tool care matters only when a supervisor is watching.
Arriving early excuses unfinished duties.
Her punctuality is positive, but responsible work also includes caring for tools.
questions.answer: Her punctuality is positive, but responsible work also includes caring for tools.
questions.explanation: A positive work attitude involves several duties. Punctuality does not replace diligence or care.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Identify responsible conduct and its consequences in a work setting.
questions.prompt: A printing assistant skips the final check to finish a job quickly. Several pages are unreadable and must be printed again. What does this show about diligence?
options: Careful checks can prevent waste and improve the useful output of work.
The fastest first attempt always produces the most useful work.
Checking work prevents any deadline from being met.
Reprinting is proof that checking was unnecessary.
questions.answer: Careful checks can prevent waste and improve the useful output of work.
questions.explanation: The skipped check caused avoidable rework. Diligence can save materials and produce usable results.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Identify responsible conduct and its consequences in a work setting.
questions.prompt: During a group project, the leader gives herself credit for a chart made by two absent classmates. Which action would best restore integrity?
options: Keep the claim because the classmates are absent.
Remove the chart from the project without explanation.
Correct the record and acknowledge the classmates who made it.
Share the credit only if the classmates complain.
questions.answer: Correct the record and acknowledge the classmates who made it.
questions.explanation: Integrity requires a truthful account of contributions even when the contributors cannot challenge the claim.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Recognise ways extended-family members can support a child's development.
questions.prompt: Tomi's aunt tells family stories and asks Tomi what the characters could have done differently. Which developmental support is clearest?
options: Replacing every lesson taught at school.
Passing on cultural knowledge while encouraging reflection on behaviour.
Proving that only adults can interpret a story.
Preventing Tomi from forming independent opinions.
questions.answer: Passing on cultural knowledge while encouraging reflection on behaviour.
questions.explanation: Discussing family stories can transmit cultural knowledge and help a child consider values and choices.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Recognise ways extended-family members can support a child's development.
questions.prompt: A cousin helps a younger child practise reading each weekend while the child's parents manage other responsibilities. What does this illustrate?
options: Extended-family support can complement care within the nuclear family.
Only parents can make a useful contribution to learning.
Children need no parental care when a cousin visits.
All extended-family members must perform the same role.
questions.answer: Extended-family support can complement care within the nuclear family.
questions.explanation: A cousin can offer learning support without replacing the parents or requiring identical roles from every relative.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain how fair treatment and cooperation promote peaceful living.
questions.prompt: Two neighbourhood groups share a meeting hall. There is no fighting, but one group is always refused a chance to speak about the booking rules. Which change would best strengthen peaceful relations?
options: Keep the exclusion because nobody has fought.
Give all future bookings to the larger group.
Cancel every meeting indefinitely.
Allow both groups to discuss fair booking rules and raise concerns respectfully.
questions.answer: Allow both groups to discuss fair booking rules and raise concerns respectfully.
questions.explanation: An inclusive and fair process addresses a source of resentment. Absence of fighting alone does not resolve exclusion.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain how fair treatment and cooperation promote peaceful living.
questions.prompt: Traders agree on a fair unloading schedule after repeated disputes at a market entrance. Deliveries then move steadily and stalls open on time. Which benefit of peaceful cooperation is shown?
options: It removes every difference of opinion.
It makes rules unnecessary.
It allows people to carry on productive activities with less disruption.
It guarantees equal earnings for every trader.
questions.answer: It allows people to carry on productive activities with less disruption.
questions.explanation: The agreement reduces disruption to ordinary work. It does not guarantee identical incomes or remove all disagreement.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain how fair treatment and cooperation promote peaceful living.
questions.prompt: A pupil says that tolerance means agreeing with every opinion in a class discussion. Which response is most accurate?
options: Tolerance means listening respectfully while retaining the right to disagree.
Tolerance requires staying silent whenever another pupil speaks.
Tolerance allows insults if an opinion seems mistaken.
Tolerance prevents anyone from giving reasons for a different view.
questions.answer: Tolerance means listening respectfully while retaining the right to disagree.
questions.explanation: Respect for other people is compatible with reasoned disagreement. Insults and forced agreement undermine discussion.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Select dialogue, compromise or mediation appropriate to a conflict.
questions.prompt: Two clubs want the school field at the same time. Without a third party deciding for them, they agree that each will use half the available time. Which method have they used?
options: Retaliation.
Compromise.
Intimidation.
Avoidance.
questions.explanation: Both clubs adjust their original demands to reach a shared agreement, which is compromise.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Select dialogue, compromise or mediation appropriate to a conflict.
questions.prompt: A teacher helps two pupils explain their disagreement, asks each to listen, and supports them in choosing their own solution. The teacher does not impose a decision. Which description fits this role?
options: Taking one pupil's side before hearing the other.
Punishing both pupils without discussing the issue.
Mediation by a person helping the parties reach agreement.
Retaliation on behalf of the class.
questions.answer: Mediation by a person helping the parties reach agreement.
questions.explanation: A mediator facilitates communication and agreement rather than imposing a settlement.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Select dialogue, compromise or mediation appropriate to a conflict.
questions.prompt: A classmate criticises Sani's plan during a calm group discussion. Which response is most likely to keep the disagreement constructive?
options: Interrupt until the classmate withdraws the criticism.
Treat the criticism as a reason to end all cooperation.
Ask friends to exclude the classmate from the group.
Ask which part causes concern, listen, and explain his own reasons calmly.
questions.answer: Ask which part causes concern, listen, and explain his own reasons calmly.
questions.explanation: Self-control and respectful dialogue let the group examine the issue without turning disagreement into personal hostility.
